scope: Proposition 14.5 (Matched caps in a finite dyadic range) of the manuscript “Strict convexity and differentiability of the planar exponential first-passage limit shape” (preprints/Strict-convexity-and-differentiability-of-the-planar-exponential-first-passage-limit-shape-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 212 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7cc30ddbfd4419f1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 77. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X(1), . . . , X(r) be finitely many required row-link templates, and let U1, . . . , Up be additional nonnegative local variables with a uni- form bound on the sum of their first moments. For every ζ > 0 and every prescribed lower bound Mprescribed, there is a fixed finite dyadic set M = {M0, 2M0, . . . , 2H−1M0}, with M0 ≥ Mprescribed, and fixed geometric tolerances, such that for every sufficiently large n some deterministic law- dependent M ∈ M satisfies, simultaneously, EfM,M (X(a) /β) ≤ ζ (1 ≤ a ≤ r), (14.22) M " r X a=1 P((X(a) /β)− > M) + p X b=1 P(Ub > M) # ≤ ζ. (14.23) In particular U1 may be the positive part of the normalized primary increment used in the road improvement.
